events.text: The tender is long dead, forty crew in a dark hull with every lamp out, and across the open hold a voice is singing. A single voice: a Choir in a crown of tuning prongs, a woman made of struck glass, standing in the middle of the cargo deck and singing the evening office to nobody. She is holding a note, and from the way the pitch hangs you can hear the chord it is waiting for, a second voice, a third. 'Compline,' she says between breaths, when she sees you. 'Forgive me, I cannot stop in the middle. There are forty of them. Everyone gets the last hour, and the chantry would not send anyone. Do you have a voice? Any voice? It need not be good.'

choices.text: Sing the third part yourself. Badly.

outcomes.text: You sing it, flat and loud and wrong, and the whole hold seems to sing with you. The hold fills with the oddest, kindest, most terrible noise you have ever heard. When the last note has rung out, Compline is crying in the way Choir cry, which is to say the glass in her chest gently hums. 'It was dreadful,' she says. 'It was perfect. Might I come with you?'
You sing, and it is as bad as it sounds. Compline waits until the end with great dignity, thanks you, and begins again from the top with her eyes shut. You tiptoe out.

choices.text: [Prismatic] Hold the third part in crystal.

outcomes.text: Your Prismatic opens their mouth and what comes out is a pure, clear, inhuman third, sitting under Compline's line like a glass floor. The chord completes. The hold seems to lean to listen. Compline sings the office through to the last note without a quaver, and when it is over she is kneeling beside your Prismatic with her prongs still ringing. 'Kin,' she says. 'I would follow that voice anywhere.'

choices.text: Light the dead their candles (2 crystal).

outcomes.text: You set two crystals in the hold as lamps, one at each end. They glow faintly in the dark, pale and patient. Compline looks at them for a long moment. 'Thank you,' she says. 'It is the first time anyone has lit them.' She finishes the office with the lamps for company, and joins you at the lock when the last note has gone.
The note follows you down the lane, long after it ought to have faded. It is probably the hull ringing. It is probably.
